title: Ordinary map reads materialize all retained save receipts
description: A household member can accumulate saved receipts through authorized edits. Once a household has a deleted object, an ordinary map read loads and parses every retained receipt, including unrelated ones. Conflict reads add another full-history pass, and the explicit history endpoint returns every receipt. Shared-process impact needs bounded local measurement and deployment context.
claimed_root_cause: The map state reader derives deleted-object type metadata by scanning and parsing the entire household save history without pagination, targeted lookup, or a persisted derived value.

trace.description: An authenticated household member invokes an ordinary map read.
The map binds actor to membership before read.
A deleted object enables receipt-history work on every map read.
Query materializes all receipt strings and loop parses each, without count or age limit.

evidence.description: Every successful nonempty save inserts map_history and a full receipt in map_save.
Conflict readState performs a second full-history parse.
Explicit history endpoint loads and parses all household receipts.
Request body limit bounds individual uploads, not accumulated history or GET work.
The 20-result cap applies to completed operation listing, not persisted receipts.
map_history has no household index or retention constraint in original schema.
History cleanup follows contentVersion change, not routine saves.

blockers: The required sandbox disk quota and artifact promotion controls were not verified, so a bounded dummy-database growth check cannot run.
The repository does not establish deployed receipt counts, concurrency, memory headroom, or ingress limits needed to determine shared availability impact.

validation_plan.local: In the required sandbox, create a small dummy household with one deleted object and increasing counts of valid small receipts. Measure GET /map latency and peak memory at bounded sizes, compare a household without deleted objects, and inspect the SQLite query plan. Stop at minimum observable growth.
validation_plan.deployment: Have the installation owner review receipt counts, memory limits, request concurrency, and ingress timeouts from private operational records to determine whether measured growth can affect other members.
